questions.question: Name two solid non-metals and describe what each looks like and where we find it.
questions.expected_answer: Carbon is black or dark grey; it is found in charcoal, coal and pencil lead (graphite). Sulfur is a pale yellow solid found near volcanoes and hot springs, and used in matches and fertilisers.

questions.question: What do dull and brittle mean? Describe a test for each.
questions.expected_answer: Dull means not shiny; we can test by looking at whether the material reflects light like a mirror when rubbed clean. Brittle means it cracks or crumbles easily when hit or bent; we can test by tapping it with a hammer inside a bag to see if it crumbles instead of flattening.

questions.question: How can you tell whether a material is a metal or a non-metal? Use the braai grid and charcoal as examples.
questions.expected_answer: Test several properties: shine, whether it can be hammered or bent without breaking, and whether it carries heat. The braai grid is shiny, bends and carries heat, so it is a metal. The charcoal is dull, crumbles and does not carry heat well, so it is a non-metal.
